question.text: 'Satyam Cat III Long-Short AIF' has a target corpus of INR 400 crore. Under SEBI (AIF) Regulations, what is the minimum sponsor / manager continuing interest?

answer.text: INR 10 crore (lower of 5% of INR 400 cr = INR 20 cr or INR 10 cr)
INR 5 crore (lower of 2.5% of INR 400 cr = INR 10 cr or INR 5 cr)

explanation.text: The Logic: For Cat III AIFs, sponsor/manager commitment = LOWER of (5% of corpus, INR 10 crore). 5% of INR 400 cr = INR 20 cr; INR 10 cr is LOWER. Hence the requirement is INR 10 crore. The Trap: Option A applies Cat I/II rule. Option C ignores the cap of INR 10 cr. Option D fabricates a 2% number. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-B explicitly tests Cat III commitments; XIX-C unifies Cat I/II and Cat III commitments — this is a favourite compare/contrast question. Manager's Pro-Tip: Cat III funds often run close to the INR 10 cr cap; negotiate with your sponsor's CFO early on cash-flow timing — the commitment must be drawn alongside LP drawdowns, not deferred to liquidation.
